item.text: The Crime and Corruption Commission surveyed community corruption perceptions to assess its prevention work and inform strategic planning.
item.support:
so the CCC can 
monitor the impact of its prevention agenda and 
inform future strategic planning.

item.text: The online survey collected 3,013 completed responses between 31 March and 20 April 2025, with results weighted by age, gender and region to reflect Queensland’s population.
item.support:
The sample was weighted to 
reflect the population statistics for age, gender and 
geographical regions.

item.text: The CCC reported that 73% saw corruption as a problem in Queensland and 78% expressed at least a fair amount of trust in the CCC.
item.support:
16% indicate 'very high' trust and a further 62% 'a fair amount of 
trust' in the organisation.

item.text: The CCC reported that 37% said they had witnessed or suspected corruption in the preceding five years, and 57% of that group had not reported it.
item.support:
Over one in three community members have either witnessed, or think 
they have witnessed, corruption in the past 5 years (37%).

item.text: The CCC identified a need for further community education about reporting processes and channels.
item.support:
Continued education is needed to inform the community on the 
process and channels for reporting corruption.

item.quote:
Continued education is needed to inform the community on the

There is some scepticism around the outcomes 
of reporting corruption; 41% agree meaningful 
action would be taken, but 23% disagree.
